56M, OBSERVATION ADMIT admission from PHYSICIAN REFERRAL.
OUTCOME: discharged alive to HOME
PRESENTING SYMPTOMS: Adult failure to thrive; Epistaxis
PRIMARY DIAGNOSIS: Multiple myeloma not having achieved remission
ACTIVE DIAGNOSES: Multiple myeloma not having achieved remission; Metabolic encephalopathy; End stage renal disease; Acute kidney failure, unspecified; Hyperuricemia without signs of inflammatory arthritis and tophaceous disease; Hyperkalemia; Other secondary thrombocytopenia; Neoplasm related pain (acute) (chronic); Type 1 diabetes mellitus without complications
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: Do not resuscitate; Acquired partial absence of pancreas; Acquired absence of spleen; Personal history of antineoplastic chemotherapy; Long term (current) use of insulin
PROCEDURES: none
MEDICATIONS: Glucose Gel 15g PO; Glucagon 1mg IM; Metoprolol Succinate XL 50mg PO; HYDROmorphone (Dilaudid) 2mg PO/NG; Creon 12 1CAP PO/NG; Dextrose 50% 12.5gm IV; Insulin 25UNIT SC; Gabapentin 100mg PO/NG; Dexamethasone 20mg PO/NG; Fentanyl Patch 12mcg/h TD; Oxymetazoline 2SPRY NU; Atovaquone Suspension 1500mg PO/NG; Sodium Chloride 0.9%  Flush 3-10mL IV; Tamsulosin 0.4mg PO; Pantoprazole 40mg PO; Neutra-Phos 2PKT PO/NG; Acyclovir 400mg PO/NG; Ramelteon 8mg PO/NG; Ondansetron ODT 4-8mg PO/NG
MICROBIOLOGY: URINE: CORYNEBACTERIUM SPECIES (DIPHTHEROIDS)
SERVICES: OMED
WARDS: Hematology/Oncology Intermediate
_patient.note:
[1] The patient is a 56-year-old male admitted from physician referral.
[2] The patient presented with adult failure to thrive and epistaxis.
[3] The patient has a primary diagnosis of multiple myeloma not having achieved remission.
[4] The patient has active diagnoses of multiple myeloma not having achieved remission, metabolic encephalopathy, end stage renal disease, acute kidney failure, unspecified, hyperuricemia without signs of inflammatory arthritis and tophaceous disease, hyperkalemia, other secondary thrombocytopenia, neoplasm related pain (acute) (chronic), and type 1 diabetes mellitus without complications.
[5] The patient has a past medical history of do not resuscitate, acquired partial absence of pancreas, acquired absence of spleen, personal history of antineoplastic chemotherapy, and long term (current) use of insulin.
[6] The patient has received no procedures.
[7] The patient is taking Glucose Gel 15g PO, Glucagon 1mg IM, Metoprolol Succinate XL 50mg PO, HYDROmorphone (Dilaudid) 2mg PO/NG, Creon 12 1CAP PO/NG, Dextrose 50% 12.5gm IV, Insulin 25UNIT SC, Gabapentin 100mg PO/NG, Dexamethasone 20mg PO/NG, Fentanyl Patch 12mcg/h TD, Oxymetazoline 2SPRY NU, Atovaquone Suspension 1500mg PO/NG, Sodium Chloride 0.9% Flush 3-10mL IV, Tamsulosin 0.4mg PO, Pantoprazole 40mg PO, Neutra-Phos 2PKT PO/NG, Acyclovir 400mg PO/NG, Ramelteon 8mg PO/NG, and Ondansetron ODT 4-8mg PO/NG.
[8] A urine culture grew Corynebacterium species (DIPHTHEROIDS).
[9] The patient was managed by the OMED service.
[10] The patient was admitted to the Hematology/Oncology Intermediate ward.
[11] The patient was discharged alive to home.
